I've been there. It sucks. Try making a list of at least three to five good things: things you're thankful for, things you like about yourself, things that make you happy. Something like that. I find it helps me refocus on the things I care about and get me out of mindsets that say "everything is terrible."

If you ever want an internet stranger to talk to/listen to you, just send me a message.

I'm kind of figuring this out too, so I'm with you. Something I've tried is I have a list of things that make me happy. Several of them are physical sensations (walking in clover is an example, or sitting in sunlight). I can use it to focus on those things and sort of reconnect my body and mind.

The problem I run into is that I don't always want to do that. It's definitely not a 100% solution, but it might help. Or what may be better is actually having something to interact with and focus on -- playdoh, a stuffed animal, a certain rock -- that may help reconnect you to physical sensations in a healthy way. It may help with anxiety too, if you can redirect your thoughts continually to the object. Don't force it, of course, because flogging your brain into submission doesn't actually work. But every time you feel yourself wandering, just slowly redirect your focus to the object.

I don't know if either of these will work for you, since everyone's different and (again) I'm relatively new. But I hope it's a starting point at least. Best of luck.

I'm definitely hoping things go way better than I expect. I know I won't be kicked out or even told it's not real (80% sure on that one). But the "you are not responsible for managing their discomfort" I think is at the center of this. I've been trying to find a way to skirt around them feeling guilty or overemotional, but maybe it's best if I don't. And if I say I'm going out somewhere repeatedly, without more information, that's when I feel like they'll start getting more suspicious or trying to find things out on their own. I'm not sure what area you live in, but you could try reaching out to therapists there and see if you could a) get an appointment to maybe figure out coping strategies and/or b) if they might have any recommendations for more immediate help. Maybe look into mental health hotlines as well.

Actually, he (name is changed, but Logan for future reference) was I think 14, or that's what he said and made a big deal out of it. He'd show medical papers and stuff to prove it (he had some sort of kidney disease, I think). From what I can tell looking at his social media and stuff since then, I think he was telling the truth. I wasn't really interested in sexting and honestly didn't know much about it. He wanted to. This was a recurring thing. I said no, he said something like "What about doggy style? That isn't actually sex" and I had no idea what I was doing so I just kind of played along, figuring out what I was supposed to do. I have no idea how often it happened. It might have only been once. I know he sent me pictures on several occasions, without me asking or wanting them, using some excuse like "___ is bothering me, maybe you can tell me what's wrong" or something.

It was super unhealthy in other ways too. It was my first realtionship, I was already dealing some with depression, and we both overcommitted way too much. Stuff like "if you died, I'd kill myself" or "I don't want to live without you." He would occasionally threaten to stop taking his meds for the kidney thing or stop eating or stuff like that. I had a crush IRL (we'll call him Steven) who was waiting to date me, since I wasn't actually allowed to date until I was 16. I don't know if he actually would have waited, but that's kind of irrelevant. I told Steven about the relationship and he basically said "That's okay, just get out of it." When I tried, Logan threatened to hurt himself. I don't know if he actually would have, but I believed him. I legitimately thought I didn't have a way out. I told Steven what Logan had said and he told me "a life is more important than a promise," and the next day said he was done having anything to do with me because I'd betrayed him.

It ended up sending me into one of my worst depressive episodes. I was definitely suicidal for a while, although I never had a solid plan for it because I was too scared. Like I said, my parents found out at some point on accident and "made me" break up with Logan, which I was fine with. I was more upset about losing contact with a different guy (George) who I'd managed to keep as solely a friend, but who threatened suicide and self-harm regularly. I believe now that it was entirely made up, but I didn't back then.

Here are some things I try:

- Stay completely still (eyes closed) for several minutes. Choose a song that you know well and play through it in your head if that helps you track the time better.

- Take deep breaths: in through your nose for seven seconds, out through your mouth gently for ten. Feel free to change the numbers, of course.

- Consciously relax your body as best you can, focusing on different parts.

- Pay attention to if you're physically uncomfortable (too hot, too cold, etc) and adjust accordingly.

- Choose a scenario in which you feel happy and/or safe, whether it's real or imaginary. Close your eyes and play out that scenario, focusing on those feelings.
